```{r}
# dependencies
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(splines)
library(car)
library(gtsummary)
library(pROC)
library(DBI)
```
### Get data

```{r}
# Connect to DuckDB mart (read-only mode)
con <- dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), dbdir = "../../sephora_products.duckdb", read_only = TRUE)

# Fetch clean data directly from your dbt mart
data1_clean <- dbGetQuery(con, "
    SELECT 
        f.product_id,
        b.brand_name,
        f.loves_count,
        f.rating,
        f.reviews_count,
        f.price_usd,
        f.is_limited_edition,
        f.is_new,
        f.is_online_only,
        f.is_out_of_stock,
        f.is_sephora_exclusive
    FROM main.fact_product_metrics f
")

# Close connection
dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)


### Clean data

#exclude products with no reviews or ratings

data1_clean <- data1_clean |>
  drop_na(rating, reviews_count, price_usd, loves_count, online_only)

# add good review cateogorical

data1_clean <- data1_clean |>
  mutate(
    good_rating = factor(
      case_when(
        rating >= 4.5 ~ 1,
        rating < 4.5 ~ 0
      ),
      levels = c(0, 1),
      labels = c("Not Good", "Good")
    )
  )

data2_clean <- data1_clean |>
  filter(
    reviews_count >= 100 & reviews_count < 10000
  )

# add log loves and log reviews
# they are super skewed

data2_clean$log_loves <- log(data2_clean$loves_count + 1)
data2_clean$log_reviews <- log(data2_clean$reviews_count + 1)

# only get sephora collection
data2_sc <- data2_clean |>
  filter(
    brand_name == "SEPHORA COLLECTION"
  )
```

### EDA

### MLR

```{r}
lm_model <- lm(loves_count ~ reviews_count + rating + price_usd + is_online_only + is_new
               , data = data2_sc)

lm2_full <- lm(
  log_loves ~ rating
  + log_reviews 
  + price_usd 
  + new 
  + online_only
  + I(log_reviews^2) 
  + log_reviews:is_new
  + log_reviews:rating
  + log_reviews:is_online_only
  + log_reviews:price_usd 
  + rating:price_usd
  + rating:is_new
  + rating:is_online_only
  , data = data2_sc
)

#summary(lm2_full)

lm_step2 <- step(lm2_full, trace=0) 
#summary(lm_step2)

vif(lm_step2, type = 'predictor')
```

```{r}
AIC(lm_model, lm2_full, lm_step2)
```

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# does it meet assumptions
plot(lm_step2, which = c(1,2))
```

### Logistic Regression - Good Rating

```{r}
glm2 <- glm(
  good_rating ~ log_loves
  + price_usd
  + is_online_only
  + is_new
  + is_out_of_stock
  + log_loves:price_usd
  , data = data2_sc
  ,family = binomial
)

#summary(glm2)
```

```{r}
glm3 <- glm(
  good_rating ~ log_loves
  + price_usd
  + log_loves:price_usd
  , data = data2_sc
  ,family = binomial
)

#summary(glm3)
vif(glm3)
```

```{r}
glm_spline <- glm(
  good_rating ~ log_loves +
                 ns(log_reviews, df = 3) +
                 price_usd +
                 is_new +
                 is_online_only +
                 is_sephora_exclusive,
  data = data2_clean,
  family = binomial
)

glm_simple <- glm(
  good_rating ~ log_loves + log_reviews,
  data = data2_sc,
  family = binomial
)

glm_linear <- glm(
  good_rating ~ log_loves + log_reviews + price_usd + is_new,
  data = data2_sc,
  family = binomial
)

glm_spline2 <- glm(
  good_rating ~ log_loves +
                 ns(log_reviews, df = 3) +
                 price_usd +
                 is_new +
                 is_online_only +
                 is_sephora_exclusive,
  data = data2_sc,  
  family = binomial
)

AIC(glm_simple, glm_linear, glm_spline2, glm2, glm3)
```

#### Cross-Validation

```{r}
set.seed(10) # set seed for reproducibility
n <- nrow(data2_sc)

# get the 70% percentile
# floor(0.7*n)

# randomly sample 70% of rows for training set
# this gets the indicies of the randomized 70% training set
train <- sample(1:n, 105) 

# fit model using training data
glm3_train <- glm(good_rating ~ log_loves + price_usd + log_loves:price_usd
                  ,data = data2_sc
                  ,subset = train
                  ,family = binomial
                  )
```

```{r}
# subset data frame for testing observations
sc_test <- data2_sc[-train, ]

# make predictions for probabilities on test set
probs_test <- predict(glm3_train, newdata = sc_test, type = "response")
```

```{r}
preds_test <- rep(0, length(probs_test)) 

# Rule for prediction
preds_test[probs_test > 0.4] <- 1
```

```{r}
tb <- table(prediction = preds_test, actual = sc_test$good_rating)
addmargins(tb)
```

```{r}
# accuracy
# the percent of correctly classified
(tb[1,1] + tb[2,2]) / 46

# sensitivity
# of the ones classified as 1, what was correctly identified as 1
# at [2,2] in the table divided by all classified as 1
tb[2,2] / 13

# specificity
# # of the ones classified as 0, what was correctly identified as 0
# at [1,1] in the table divided by all classified as 0
tb[1,1] / 33
```

```{r}
# x axis = 1 - specificity # misclassification of 1s
# y axis = sensitivity
# would want x = 0 and y = 1 or as close as possible
library(pROC)
require(pROC)
roc_obj <- roc(sc_test$good_rating, probs_test)

plot(roc_obj, print.auc = TRUE, legacy.axes = TRUE)
```

```{r}
coords(roc_obj, "best")
```
